name: Criminal Justice (Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing) Acts 2010-2021
reference: Act No. 6 of 2010 (as amended by 2013, 2018, 2021 Acts)
supervisor: Central Bank of Ireland (FIs) + Department of Justice + Revenue + professional bodies

articles.title: Designated persons
articles.requirement: Designated persons obligated under the Acts include: credit + financial institutions; auditors + external accountants + tax advisers + insolvency practitioners; legal professionals (when carrying out specified financial / property / corporate transactions); trust + company service providers; estate agents; property service providers; dealers in goods accepting cash payments of €10,000+; high-value goods dealers (≥€10,000); gambling operators; virtual asset service providers (transitioning to MiCA CASPs).

articles.title: Business risk assessment
articles.requirement: A designated person must carry out an assessment of the risks of money laundering + terrorist financing involved in the carrying on of business by it as a designated person; document; keep up to date; reflect risk factors including customer, product, service, transaction, delivery channel, geographic + new technologies.

articles.title: Customer due diligence — application
articles.requirement: CDD measures applied: at establishment of a business relationship; carrying out an occasional transaction of €15,000+ (or €1,000+ for wire transfers); on suspicion of money laundering / terrorist financing irrespective of any threshold; where there are doubts about the veracity or adequacy of previously obtained CDD information.

articles.title: CDD measures
articles.requirement: CDD measures: identify + verify the customer using documents / data / information from reliable + independent sources; identify the beneficial owner + take reasonable measures to verify; obtain information on the purpose + intended nature of the relationship; conduct ongoing monitoring (transaction scrutiny + record refresh).

articles.title: Enhanced due diligence
articles.requirement: EDD required for: high-risk third countries; complex / unusual / large transactions with no apparent economic purpose; situations representing a higher risk of money laundering or terrorist financing (assessed by reference to risk factors at s.30A). Senior management approval to enter / continue; documented rationale; enhanced monitoring.

articles.title: PEPs — domestic + foreign
articles.requirement: Enhanced measures for foreign + domestic + international-organisation PEPs + family members + close associates: senior management approval; source of wealth + source of funds checks; ongoing enhanced monitoring. PEP status continues 12 months after the person ceases to hold the prominent public function.

articles.title: Suspicious Transaction Reporting (STRs)
articles.requirement: A designated person who knows, suspects or has reasonable grounds to suspect that another person has been or is engaged in money laundering / terrorist financing shall, as soon as practicable, report the suspicion to the Garda Síochána FIU + Revenue. Statutory immunity for good-faith reports. Tipping-off prohibition under s.49.

articles.title: Tipping-off prohibition
articles.requirement: Designated person commits an offence by disclosing to a third party that an STR has been filed, or that an investigation may be carried out. Carve-outs for legal advice + within the same legal entity + with regulators.

articles.title: Internal policies + procedures + controls
articles.requirement: Designated persons must adopt internal policies, controls + procedures to prevent + detect ML/TF, including: customer + business risk assessment + their application; CDD; reliance on third parties; reporting; record retention (5 years minimum); monitoring transactions; staff vetting + training. Reviewed regularly; approved at senior level.

articles.title: Group-wide programmes
articles.requirement: Designated persons that are part of a group must apply group-wide AML/CFT policies + procedures at branch + majority-owned subsidiary level, including information-sharing for ML/TF purposes within group + group-level CDD.

articles.title: EU AMLR transition + readiness
articles.requirement: From 10 July 2027 the EU AMLR (directly applicable) governs CDD, EDD, PEPs, beneficial-ownership identification + similar customer-facing AML obligations. The CJMLA framework will be partially superseded; the AMLD6 + AMLA Authority cooperation framework will be transposed via further Irish legislation. Designated persons should plan for: harmonised CDD documentation, AMLA direct supervision for highest-risk obliged entities (from 2028), and the centralised EU-level information-sharing framework.
